page: Google Cloud Platform x4-960-12t-metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server built for ultra-large computing environments. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 960 dedicated vCPUs and 12,288 GB of system memory. This configuration establishes a memory density of 12.8 GB per core, positioning it at the upper echelon of single-node memory allocations within the GCP catalog.

The instance does not include integrated graphical accelerators or bundled local storage volumes. System architectures deployed on this server rely entirely on attached network storage for persistent filesystems and operating volumes. Additionally, the instance provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating dedicated network routing or private connectivity for ingress and egress traffic.

From an efficiency standpoint, the consolidation of 960 dedicated cores and 12 terabytes of RAM onto bare metal minimizes virtualization overhead and facilitates high utilization per node. Tradeoffs involve managing external storage throughput and latency, as storage performance depends strictly on remote infrastructure. The server is suited for enterprise in-memory databases, such as large-scale SAP HANA deployments, massive transactional data grids, and extreme-scale analytics workloads requiring multi-terabyte working memory.
description: Google Cloud Platform x4-960-12t-metal is a bare-metal server in the memory-optimized family engineered for extreme-scale computing. Driven by the x86_64 architecture, this instance supplies 960 dedicated vCPUs alongside 12,288 GB of total system RAM, establishing an allocation ratio of 12.8 GB of memory per core. The configuration operates without integrated GPUs and contains no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached persistent disks or external storage systems to accommodate data persistence. It also provisions zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Due to its dense physical compute core count and massive multi-terabyte memory footprint, the server delivers high cost efficiency when consolidating sprawling enterprise infrastructures onto unified bare-metal hardware. Architectural tradeoffs center on managing network-dependent storage latency and external bandwidth. The system is structurally fitted for multi-terabyte in-memory database environments, such as large SAP HANA workloads, real-time transactional analytics engines, and vast in-memory data caches.
